content.title: About
content.content: Cuban coffee is a fragrant Arabica variety grown on Cuban plantations. It is known for its rich, slightly sweet flavor with notes of chocolate and nuts. Traditionally it is roasted to a medium level to preserve its fruity and caramel undertones.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cuban coffee began export in the early 1920s, becoming a key part of the island’s economy.
Most plantations are located in the mountainous Sierra Maestra region, where the climate is ideal for Arabica.
Cuban baristas often serve coffee with sugar but without milk to highlight its natural aroma.
During the 1959 revolution coffee production dropped sharply, but the industry revived in the 1990s.
Cuban coffee is frequently used as the base for the cocktail “Cuba Libre” for added flavor.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Improves focus
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, enhancing attention and reaction time.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Moderate coffee intake can boost metabolic rate and aid fat burning.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Studies link regular moderate coffee consumption with reduced risk of Parkinson’s disease and some cancers.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after coffee.

items.title: Increased stomach acidity
items.content: Coffee can aggravate gastritis and reflux symptoms in susceptible people.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain medications, such as antidepressants.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit caffeine intake to about 200 mg per day.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cuban coffee is usually brewed as espresso or filtered coffee, served hot, often with a small amount of sugar. It can be used as a base for lattes, cappuccinos, or cold coffee drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ground coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. For longer storage, use vacuum‑sealed bags or keep it in the refrigerator, but consume within 2–3 months.
